examGuideline.title: ASCP BOC HT/HTL Examination Content Guideline

difficultyDefinitions.Foundational: Recall or explain a core fact, sequence, reagent, structure, or principle.
difficultyDefinitions.Application: Apply a principle to select a method, control, reagent, or next step.
difficultyDefinitions.Troubleshooting: Interpret a failure pattern and choose the most appropriate corrective action.

fixation-v3.title: Fixation
outlineTopics: Tissue morphology, anatomy, preservation, pathology, and HTL biochemistry
Fixation procedures for routine, frozen, special-stain, IHC, IF, cytology, and ISH workflows
Specimen size, fixative volume, time, temperature, pH, reagents, artifacts, instrumentation, and quality control
fixation-v3.htlEmphasis: Pathology, biochemistry and chemistry principles, and the effect of fixation on advanced staining and molecular targets.
references: ASCP BOC HT/HTL Examination Content Guideline, revised December 5, 2025.
ASCP BOC HT/HTL Suggested Reading for Examination Preparation.
Carson FL, Cappellano CH. Histotechnology: A Self-Instructional Text. 5th ed. ASCP Press; 2020.
Brown RW, ed. Histologic Preparations: Common Problems and Their Solutions. College of American Pathologists; 2009.
Bancroft JD, Gamble M, eds. Theory and Practice of Histological Techniques. 8th ed.

processing-v3.title: Processing and Decalcification
outlineTopics: Tissue morphology and component preservation during reagent exchange
Routine, frozen, enzyme, calcified/decalcified, IHC, IF, cytology, and ISH processing procedures
Processor components, use, maintenance, troubleshooting, reagent chemistry, and quality control
processing-v3.htlEmphasis: Chemistry principles, preservation for advanced assays, and selection of processing and decalcification methods.
references: ASCP BOC HT/HTL Examination Content Guideline, revised December 5, 2025.
ASCP BOC HT/HTL Suggested Reading for Examination Preparation.
Carson FL, Cappellano CH. Histotechnology: A Self-Instructional Text. 5th ed. ASCP Press; 2020.
Bancroft JD, Gamble M, eds. Theory and Practice of Histological Techniques. 8th ed.
Brown RW, ed. Histologic Preparations: Common Problems and Their Solutions. College of American Pathologists; 2009.

embedding-v3.title: Embedding and Microtomy
outlineTopics: Tissue morphology, anatomy, orientation, and component demonstration
Paraffin, frozen-section, gelatin/adhesive, and quality-control procedures
Microtome, water-bath, cryostat, maintenance, troubleshooting, and HTL molecular-testing preparation
embedding-v3.htlEmphasis: Preparation of sections for molecular testing, including RNA-aware handling, scrolls, and specialized sampling concepts.
references: ASCP BOC HT/HTL Examination Content Guideline, revised December 5, 2025.
ASCP BOC HT/HTL Suggested Reading for Examination Preparation.

he-guide.title: Routine H&E Staining
outlineTopics: Nuclear and cytoplasmic morphology, anatomy, function, pathology, and HTL biochemistry
Hematoxylin and eosin procedures, reagent and dye properties, instrumentation, mounting, and quality control
Troubleshooting differentiation, bluing, eosin balance, dehydration, clearing, and coverslipping
he-guide.htlEmphasis: Biochemistry and chemistry principles, pathology correlation, and quality-system decisions affecting stain performance.
references: ASCP BOC HT/HTL Examination Content Guideline, revised December 5, 2025.

special-stains.title: Special Stains
outlineTopics: Carbohydrates, connective/supporting tissue, lipids, microorganisms, nerve, pigments, minerals, granules, fibrin, and mast cells
Target chemistry, expected colors, control selection, preliminary screening, and quality control
Reagent and dye properties, instrumentation, differentiation, mounting, artifacts, and troubleshooting
special-stains.htlEmphasis: Pathology and biochemistry correlation, enzyme histochemistry, preliminary screening, and higher-level control selection.

lab-operations.title: Laboratory Operations
outlineTopics: Safety, chemical storage, disposal, hazards, procedures, regulations, and quality control
Metric, percent-solution, dilution, and molar-solution calculations
Ancillary equipment, maintenance, troubleshooting, management, education, federal regulation, and accrediting agencies

ihc-ish.title: IHC and ISH Fundamentals
outlineTopics: IHC principles, retrieval, controls, antibody preparation, detection, instrumentation, quality control, and troubleshooting
In situ hybridization, including FISH and CISH, and preservation across fixation and processing
HTL-level assay validation, control selection, chemistry, pathology correlation, and preparation for molecular testing
ihc-ish.htlEmphasis: Detailed immunostaining principles, control selection, antibody preparation, ISH, validation, lot bridging, and molecular preservation.
references: ASCP BOC HT/HTL Examination Content Guideline, revised December 5, 2025.
